description: Practitioner mental models / decision frameworks (Buffett's investing, Musk's first-principles, Munger's mental models, leadership archetypes). Heuristic + case-study > theory derivation.

frontier_definition.currency_signal: primary sources by named author — letters, talks, interviews, public writings
frontier_definition.prompt_anchor: Frontier here is undated — it's the practitioner's own primary writings. Cite specific letters, interviews, books, talks BY NAME and DATE. Avoid third-party commentary unless it's the only source.

phases.label: Origin
phases.tone: the formative experience that produced this way of thinking; what the practitioner reacts against; the world they came up in

phases.label: Decisions
phases.tone: the canonical case studies — the trades / launches / calls / writings that defined them; situational detail by name and date

phases.label: Heuristics
phases.tone: the rules-of-thumb they applied, in their own words where possible; the latticework / checklists / mental models they reach for

phases.label: Edge cases
phases.tone: where their model breaks; documented failure modes; strongest critics; situations the framework doesn't fit

phases.label: Synthesis
phases.tone: the learner's own framework re-derived from the practitioner's — applied to a problem the practitioner never faced
